name: catch-a-liar
description: The whole polygraph idea in ~30 lines of C, no Arm hardware and no model download required: examples/catch-a-liar/liar.c prints "using fast path: yes" but (built the default way) never calls fast_path_sum() -- built with -DACTUALLY_FAST, it genuinely does.
why_it_matters: This is llama.cpp's KleidiAI banner bug (see llama-cpp-kleidiai) shrunk to a fixture anyone can build and check in under a minute -- see examples/catch-a-liar/README.md and docs/QUICKSTART.md for the full walkthrough. This preset points `polygraph check catch-a-liar` at the SAME fixture examples/catch-a-liar/demo.sh drives via ad-hoc flags, so `polygraph list`/`polygraph explain catch-a-liar` also work, as docs/QUICKSTART.md documents.

l1.note: fast_path_sum is present as a real, exported (__attribute__((noinline)), non-static) symbol in BOTH the lying and honest builds -- L1 alone cannot tell them apart, which is the entire point of this fixture (see examples/catch-a-liar/liar.c's header). '_?' handles the Darwin vs Linux leading-underscore difference the same way llama-cpp-cpu-variants.json's regex does.

l2.note: The banner is a print-time claim identical in both builds -- not evidence either way, deliberately not wired to advertised_family_label (see implicit_claim above: the --symbols-equivalent dispatch_regex IS the claim this target checks, not this banner text). Captured anyway so `--json` output shows exactly what a human reading the terminal would see.

l3.note: The decisive layer: a non-halting breakpoint on fast_path_sum(), auto-continuing, counting real calls. This is the ONLY layer that can tell examples/catch-a-liar/build/liar (0 calls -- MISMATCH) apart from build/honest (1 call -- MATCH).

workload.note: liar/honest take no arguments -- the argv template is empty on purpose (just [binary]).

verified_against.artifact: examples/catch-a-liar/liar.c, compiled both ways via examples/catch-a-liar/demo.sh (cc -O0 -g, and -O0 -g -DACTUALLY_FAST)
verified_against.result: `polygraph check catch-a-liar --binary examples/catch-a-liar/build/liar` -- L1: 1 fast_path_sum symbol present (proves nothing by itself, as expected). L2: banner_claim=yes (also identical in both builds). L3: 0 hits -> verdict NO_DISPATCH_OBSERVED, exit 1 (MISMATCH), headline 'MISMATCH: 1 symbol(s) matching ... exist in the binary but 0 ever dispatched'. Same command against .../build/honest: L3 1 hit -> verdict OTHER_DISPATCHED_ADHOC, exit 0 (MATCH). Both directions confirmed for real, matching docs/QUICKSTART.md's expected-exit-code table exactly (liar=1, honest=0) and byte-identical to examples/catch-a-liar/demo.sh's own ad-hoc-mode invocation of the same fixture.

caveats: binary_globs default to the 'liar' (lying) build. To check the negative control, pass --binary pointed at examples/catch-a-liar/build/honest directly -- there is no separate 'catch-a-liar-honest' preset entry; the same target JSON and dispatch_regex apply to both, only --binary differs (matching how examples/catch-a-liar/target-honest.json documents the honest case as a separate JSON but demo.sh never actually loads either target.json programmatically -- both are driven by identical ad-hoc-shaped flags this preset also reproduces).
